meta.title: Thank you — we have your request · Ride Fleet
meta.description: Your demo request is in. We confirm by email the same business day. Here is what happens next and what is worth having ready for the call.

thankYou.title: Thank you. Your request is in
thankYou.lede: Someone on the team reviews it and writes to you to set the date. In the meantime, here is what happens next, what is worth having ready, and where to read on.

next.title: What happens next

0.title: Confirmation by email
0.body: We reply the same business day with two or three times to choose from. If you wrote outside working hours, the clock starts on the next business day.

1.title: We set up the call
1.body: The confirmation email carries the date, the time with its time zone, the language the call will be held in, and the link to join.

2.title: Half an hour about your operation
2.body: We go through how you work today, show you the product live, and finish with concrete next steps. No obligation and no filler slides.

next.reminderNote: For now the only reminder goes out by email.

prep.title: What is worth having ready
prep.lede: None of this is required. The more concrete the starting point, the more you get out of the half hour.

items.0: How many vehicles you run today, and how many you expect to run in twelve months.
items.1: How the business operates: traditional rental, dealership loaners, or a mix.
items.2: Which toll accounts you use, AutoExpreso or SunPass, and how you reconcile tolls today.
items.3: What you work with now: spreadsheets, a booking system, accounting software.
items.4: Who answers the phone after hours, and how many calls go unanswered.
items.5: The number you want to move: tolls recovered, office hours, calls answered.

change.title: If something needs to change
change.body: Wrong detail, need a different date, or want to cancel: write to us and we will fix it. Replying to the confirmation works too.

onward.title: In the meantime
onward.lede: If you want to arrive with context, these are the three modules.
onward.rfm: The operations spine: reservations, contracts, handovers and returns in one place.
onward.toll: AutoExpreso and SunPass tolls collected and matched to the right contract.
onward.voz: The AI front desk that answers calls on your behalf and handles the scheduling.

pickup.title: The customer lands, calls, and the shuttle goes
pickup.lede: Somebody who has just picked up their bag does not want a form: they want a ride. They call, Valet identifies the reservation, and the request lands on the floor. In the product it shows up as shuttle requests.

0.body: The assistant searches by confirmation number, tolerating each booking channel's prefix and what gets lost when a code is read out over a phone. If that fails, it searches by name within a date window.

1.value: The assistant can only ask for the pickup
1.body: It can create the request and nothing else. It cannot see the queue, mark it complete, cancel it or record a no-show. Closing a shuttle is a human act, and an automated test insists on it.

2.value: A customer at the curb outranks any screen
2.body: The notice appears over whatever screen the agent is on, with the name, the reservation, how many they are and how long they have waited. A second call marks the row and raises a counter instead of creating a duplicate.

trust.title: The delicate part is not sending the shuttle, it is not reading somebody else's reservation to whoever called
trust.body: If the code does not match exactly, the assistant does not get the reservation: it gets a first name, a last initial and the month of the pickup, and nothing more. Unmasking it takes a detail the search did not already use, and the detail that found someone can never be the one that proves it is them. In doubt, it stays masked. And the limit that stops blind guessing is tuned not to punish the most common failure on a call, a misheard code: if that counted against you, an honest customer would pay for a noisy line.

tracker.title: Your shuttle, live
tracker.body: Every customer gets a personal link to watch the shuttle move on the map, know exactly where to stand and wait for it, and request it with one tap.

0.body: Twenty-four hours before pickup, by email and text message. Personal, tied to their reservation, and alive until the rental ends, so it serves the return trip too. Nothing to install and nothing to type.

1.body: The shuttle moving, a pin on the exact waiting spot, and the instructions your branch wrote. If they share their location they see how far they still have to walk. And they switch between Spanish and English with one tap.

2.body: One button, and the request lands on the branch team's screen. If they also phone in, or tap twice, it does not become two requests: it stays one bus.

0.alt: Phone screen with the map: the shuttle marked over the airport, a LIVE badge, and below it the branch, the frequency and where to wait.
0.caption: The map, with the shuttle and the waiting spot.

1.alt: The same map with the customer's location: a blue dot, a line to the waiting spot, and the text You are 360 metres from the pickup spot.
1.caption: Share your location and see the walk left.

2.alt: The card with no map: the shuttle is not transmitting right now, service is still running, and the request button is still available.
2.caption: No signal says so, and the button stays.

tracker.shotsNote: Demonstration screens over simulated data, not a live operation.

privacy.title: There is no public link to your fleet
privacy.body: There is no fixed address here and no code anyone can paste anywhere: each link is personal, tied to one reservation, and it expires. What it shows is deliberately trimmed, with an automated test watching the list: where the shuttle is and where to wait, without the customer's name, without the reservation number, without their phone and without the plate. The GPS is not even queried while nobody has the map open and nobody is waiting.

items.0: The map needs a GPS unit fitted to the shuttle. Without that hardware the page still exists, but it shows no position.
items.1: There is no ETA. Nothing computes one, and the frequency on screen is a number your admin typed.
items.2: It does not assign a driver. Nobody is bound to the request: a person reads the notice and dispatches.
items.3: The dot on the map is routinely fifteen to thirty seconds behind, and the page keeps calling it live for up to a minute and a half. When the signal is genuinely lost it says so, rather than leaving a stale dot up.
items.4: The line to the waiting spot is direction and distance, not turn-by-turn navigation.
items.5: The link is personal and it expires, but it works for whoever holds it: if your customer forwards it, that person sees the same map.
items.6: It does not escalate on its own. If nobody works the queue the notice simply stays up; there is no time-based alert and no supervisor ping.

pickup.close: Check-out closes the request by itself, in the same transaction that hands the car over. Nobody has to remember.

meta.title: Pricing · Ride Fleet
meta.description: What you pay depends on the size of your fleet and the modules you switch on. We give you the number on the call, not in a generic table.

pricing.title: You get the number on the call
pricing.lede: We do not publish a price table, and we would rather say why: what you pay depends on how many units you run and which modules you switch on. A generic table would waste your time and ours.

0.body: Ten units and four hundred are not the same operation or the same support load, and they should not cost the same.

1.body: Ride Fleet Manager is the base. Toll Bridge and Valet switch on if you need them, and there is a market-pricing add-on that is billed separately.

2.body: An operator at one airport and one with branches across two markets are not carrying the same system. Standing up each market is real work.

included.title: What is included, said before you ask
included.body: Training your team through Ride University is not billed separately: it comes with the product, with the whole syllabus in Spanish and English, because a system your staff cannot work is not worth what it costs. The market-intelligence add-on is billed separately, and we tell you how much on the same call.
included.note: We do not charge to set your people up, or by how many of them you train.

cta.title: Half an hour, and you leave with the number
cta.body: Tell us how many units you run and how you operate. On the call we give you the price, and if we are not right for you we say so there rather than chasing you for three weeks.

meta.title: Security and data handling · Ride Fleet
meta.description: Where the data lives, how it is encrypted, who can see it, how it is backed up, and what we do not have yet. No claims to certifications we do not hold.

security.title: How we handle data
security.lede: This page describes today, not an ambition. Ride Fleet is a young company: some things are settled and some are not, and both are written here.

noCert.title: First, plainly
noCert.body: Ride Fleet holds no SOC 2, no ISO 27001 and no HIPAA certification, and has not been through an external security audit. If your buying process requires one of those today, we cannot satisfy it yet. We would rather say so on this page than across a table.

holdings.title: What data we hold today
holdings.body: This marketing site hosts no customer operational data. The only thing it receives is demo requests: name, company, email, optional phone, fleet size, business model, notes, and where the visit came from.
holdings.link: The full detail is in the privacy policy

hosting.title: Where the data lives
hosting.body: The site and its services run on cloud infrastructure hosted in United States regions, which is where the business operates: Puerto Rico and the mainland. There are no copies in other regions.
hosting.pendingBody: The hosting decision is still in progress. As soon as it closes, the provider and the region are named here with a date.

transit.title: Encryption in transit
transit.body: All traffic travels over HTTPS with TLS. No form or endpoint is served unencrypted, and the secure channel is enforced on every response.

rest.title: Encryption at rest
rest.body: The disks holding the data are encrypted at rest by the infrastructure provider, with keys managed by that provider and rotation on its side.
rest.vault: Encrypted vault for toll portal credentials
rest.vaultBody: Toll Bridge needs credentials for each toll authority you use. The design is a vault with per-customer encryption, credentials that are never shown in full on screen, and a record of every use. That module is being built, and until it runs with a customer in production we are not going to call it finished.

access.title: Who can see what
access.body: Access is granted per person and only where it is needed.

items.0: Named accounts, one per person, no shared credentials.
items.1: Second factor required on every infrastructure administration account.
items.2: Least privilege: nobody holds production access by default.
items.3: Access is revoked the same day somebody leaves the team.

access.auditBody: Being able to check for yourself who on our side touched your data, and when, is part of the product and is not available yet.

backups.title: Backups and recovery
backups.body: Backups are taken automatically and encrypted by the database provider, with a rolling retention window and point-in-time restore.
backups.gap: Documented restore test, with published RPO and RTO
backups.gapBody: Having backups is not the same as having timed a restore. That test and its numbers are not documented yet.

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
subprocessors.body: We use outside providers to host infrastructure, deliver transactional email, and carry voice and text messages. None of them receives customer operational data today, because there are no customers in production yet.
subprocessors.listBody: It gets published on this page, with provider, purpose and country, before the first customer's data is processed. Until then, ask us by email and we send it as it stands.

incident.title: Incidents and reports
incident.body: If you find something that looks like a vulnerability or misuse, write to us and we treat it as a priority. Nothing needs to be signed to report, and we take no legal action against anyone reporting in good faith.
incident.commitment: If an incident ever affects a customer's data, we tell that customer directly with what we know, even while the investigation is still open.
incident.policy: Incident response policy with published timelines
incident.policyBody: The internal procedure exists in draft. The committed timelines get published here once they have been reviewed.

notYet.title: What we do not have yet
notYet.lede: This list exists so nobody has to guess.

items.0: An external security audit and a third-party penetration test.
items.2: A public service status page with incident history.
items.3: A published data processing agreement that can be signed online.

notYet.close: When any of these changes, this page changes, and so does its date.

contact.title: Security questions
contact.body: If you are evaluating Ride Fleet and need answers for your buying process, write to us. We answer with what exists, including when the answer is "not yet".

legal.draftNote: Draft under legal review. This document describes what we do today and may change before launch. When it changes, the date changes with it.

meta.title: Privacy policy · Ride Fleet
meta.description: What this site collects, what it is used for, how long it is kept, and how to ask us to delete it.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lede: This site collects little, and states all of it. If anything here is unclear, write to us and we will explain it in ordinary words.

who.title: Who we are
who.body: Ride Fleet is a software company for fleet operators, based in San Juan, Puerto Rico. We are responsible for the data sent through this site, and we answer at the email address at the end of this page.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body: There is only one way to give us personal data on this site: sending the demo form. The rest is generated by the server as it serves the page.

items.0: What you type into the form: name, company, work email, optional phone, role, fleet size, business model, products of interest, preferred language and notes.
items.1: The consent confirmation you tick when you submit the form.
items.2: Where the visit came from: campaign parameters, landing page, and the referring site if there is one.
items.3: Technical server logs: IP address, browser type and request time, generated automatically.
items.4: We do not collect special category data, data about children, or payment information on this site.

items.0: Answering your request and setting up the demo.
items.1: Understanding which channels bring useful conversations, so we do not spend on the ones that do not.
items.2: Keeping the site available and protected against abuse.
items.3: We do not sell data, do not pass it to data brokers, and make no automated decisions about you.

basis.title: On what basis we process it
basis.body: We process your data because you sent it to us so we would get in touch, and because you ticked the consent box. You can withdraw that consent at any time, without explaining why.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body: Demo requests are kept for as long as the commercial conversation runs, and up to twenty-four months after the last contact. Technical server logs last a short operational period. If you ask for deletion, it happens sooner.

sharing.title: Who we share it with
sharing.body: With the providers we need in order to operate: site hosting, email delivery, and, once it is connected, the customer management system. None is connected today, so requests sit in the application logs until somebody answers you. We may also share information where a law or a court order requires it.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can ask for the following about the data we hold on you.

items.0: A copy of what we hold.
items.1: Correction of anything that is wrong.
items.3: Withdrawal of consent and removal from our emails.
items.4: An objection to your data being used for marketing.

rights.after: Write to us and we answer through the same channel. We do not charge for handling these requests.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: This site uses no marketing, advertising or social network cookies. The detail is on the cookies page.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If what we collect, or what we use it for, changes, this text is updated along with its date. Material changes are also sent to anyone who has already written to us.

contact.title: How to reach us
contact.body: For anything about privacy, including deletion of your data, write to:

meta.title: Terms of use · Ride Fleet
meta.description: The conditions this site is offered under: what is informational, what is not a contract, and who to write to.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lede: The site's rules, in the plainest language we could write them in.

scope.title: What these terms cover
scope.body: They cover use of this marketing site. They do not cover use of the product: that is governed by the separate signed agreement, which prevails over this page wherever it applies.

informational.title: The site is informational
informational.body: Product descriptions, screens and examples illustrate where Ride Fleet is going. Anything marked as being built is not available yet. Nothing on this site is a binding offer or a promise that a feature will exist on a given date.

sample.title: Sample data
sample.body: The product screens shown on the site are renderings built from invented data. They are not a customer's screen and contain nobody's information.

acceptable.title: Acceptable use
acceptable.body: By using the site, you agree not to do the following.

items.0: Attempt to reach systems, accounts or data without authorization.
items.1: Extract content automatically at a scale that degrades the service for everyone else.
items.2: Submit false details, or somebody else's details, through the forms.
items.3: Use the site for anything illegal or to harass others.
items.4: Extract this site's content, by any automated means, to train artificial-intelligence models or build datasets. That right is expressly reserved, and the reservation does not depend on whether a crawler honours our robots.txt.

ip.title: Intellectual property
ip.body: The content, design, code and marks on this site belong to Ride Fleet. You may quote extracts with attribution and a link; copying whole pages, or using our marks in a way that suggests our endorsement, you may not.

thirdParty.title: Third-party marks
thirdParty.body: AutoExpreso, SunPass, E-PASS, FasTrak and any other third-party names belong to their owners. We name them to describe compatibility and integration. That implies no affiliation, sponsorship or endorsement by those entities.

warranty.title: No warranty on the site
warranty.body: The site is offered as is. We take care that the information is correct and that the site stays up, but we do not warrant that it is free of errors or interruptions.

liability.title: Limitation of liability
liability.body: To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for indirect or incidental damages arising from use of this site. None of this limits liability that the law does not permit to be limited.

links.title: Links to other sites
links.body: When we link to a third-party site it is for reference. We do not control its content or its privacy practices.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.body: We may update them. The version in force is always the one published here, with its date.

law.title: Governing law
law.body: These terms are governed by the laws of the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and any dispute is heard in the courts of San Juan.

contact.title: How to reach us
contact.body: For questions about these terms, write to:

meta.title: Cookies and local storage · Ride Fleet
meta.description: What this site stores in your browser. Today: nothing for analytics or advertising. Here is the detail, and what would change if we add measurement.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.lede: The short version: this site does not track you today. The long version is below.

today.title: What is here today
today.body: This site sets no analytics, advertising or social network cookies. There are no third-party pixels, no remarketing tags, and no scripts that follow you to other sites.

essential.title: Strictly necessary storage
essential.body: The infrastructure provider may set technical cookies for security, load balancing and abuse protection. They are not used to profile you and are not used for marketing.

language.title: Your language
language.body: The language preference travels in the page address, in the /es or /en prefix, not in a cookie. The ES | EN control takes you to the same page in the other language without storing anything in your browser.

analytics.title: Measurement
analytics.badgeBody: If we ever turn on analytics, it will be aggregate measurement behind a consent notice in Spanish and English, where declining is as visible as accepting.
analytics.body: Until that notice exists and works, no measurement tag is loaded. This page is updated the same day that changes.

control.title: How to control them
control.body: Your browser lets you inspect, block and delete cookies site by site, and private mode discards them on close. Blocking the strictly necessary ones may stop the site from loading properly.

forms.title: Forms are a different matter
forms.body: What you send through the demo form is not a cookie: it is data you hand over deliberately, and it is governed by the privacy policy.

contact.title: How to reach us
contact.body: For questions about cookies or measurement, write to:

meta.title: Accessibility statement · Ride Fleet
meta.description: Our target is WCAG 2.2 level AA. Here is what has been verified, what is missing, and how to tell us if you hit a barrier.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.lede: If you cannot use something on this site, that is a defect on our side and we want to hear about it.

target.title: The target
target.body: This site is built to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, WCAG 2.2, level AA, equally in Spanish and English. Accessibility is reviewed as part of the work on each page, not at the end.

status.title: Conformance status
status.body: Partially conformant. We meet most level AA criteria, and the known exceptions are written out below without decoration.

items.0: Text and icon contrast was measured against the level AA thresholds. Combinations that fell short were corrected in the design system before publishing.
items.1: The whole site can be navigated by keyboard, with a skip-to-content link and a visible focus indicator on every control.
items.2: The focus indicator uses its own color, distinct from the brand color, so it stands out on any background.
items.3: Semantic structure: one H1 per page, headings in order, and labeled landmark regions.
items.4: Every control has a programmatic name. Buttons that show only an icon carry text for screen readers.
items.5: Icons are decorative graphics and the meaning always sits in the text beside them. No emoji are used anywhere.
items.6: The language attribute changes with the language of the page, so screen readers pronounce it correctly.
items.7: The system preference for reduced motion is respected.
items.8: Blocks that open and close use native browser elements, operable by keyboard without depending on JavaScript.

gaps.title: What is missing
gaps.lede: Verification so far has been internal. That has limits, and here they are.

items.0: We have not run an external audit or testing with people who use assistive technology daily.
items.1: There are no automated accessibility tests running on each publish yet.
items.2: There is no audio or video on the site. When there is, it will carry captions and a transcript from day one.

gaps.schedulerBody: When one is integrated, its accessibility is validated before it is published, and the form stays available as an equivalent alternative route.

barriers.title: If you hit a barrier
barriers.body: Write to us and tell us which page it was on, what you were trying to do, and what happened. If you use a screen reader, magnification or a large text size, say so as well: it helps us reproduce the problem.
barriers.promise: We answer, we fix what can be fixed quickly, and in the meantime we give you another way to finish what you were doing, by email or by phone.

contact.title: How to reach us
contact.body: To report a barrier or ask for content in another format, write to:
